title: A domain with factorizations into irreducibles is a UFD exactly when every irreducible is prime

standard_prerequisites.name: Unique factorization read on products of irreducibles
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the first half of the counted proof (lines 29651-29660)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets a single irreducible appearing in a product be recognised as an associate of one of the factors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction on the total number of irreducible factors
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces uniqueness of two factorizations to the case of one fewer factor on each side.

core_obligations: If R is a UFD, show every irreducible is prime: from ab in (x) factor the three elements into irreducibles and use uniqueness to see that x is an associate of one of the factors, so a or b lies in (x) (proof lines 29651-29660).

Conversely, assuming every irreducible is prime, take two factorizations into irreducibles and use primality of the first irreducible to move one factor from the right side to an associate on the left (proof lines 29663-29669).
Cancel that pair and finish by induction on the total number of factors (proof lines 29669-29671).
proof_roadmap: Turn unique factorization into primality of irreducibles (proof lines 29650-29660).
Turn primality of irreducibles into uniqueness of factorizations by induction (proof lines 29662-29673).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a domain in which every nonzero nonunit factors into irreducibles, being a unique factorization domain is equivalent to every irreducible element being prime (statement lines 29643-29648). The proof does not build the divisor theory: one direction factors a product equality into irreducibles and uses uniqueness to say that the chosen irreducible is an associate of one of the factors, and the other direction takes two factorizations, uses primality of one irreducible to match a factor on the other side, cancels the pair and concludes by induction on the total number of factors (proof lines 29650-29673). The matching-and-cancelling step is the substance, and the author writes both directions in full. H2.
